headline: CORN HOLDS $5 AS GRAIN STOCKS COME IN HEAVY
lead: Corn traded at $5.00 overnight, up 3 cents from Monday's $4.97¼ settle, even after USDA's Grain Stocks report put old-crop corn bushels at 2.10 billion, up 35% from a year ago. Soybeans added a nickel to $12.86 on a 3% stocks draw the other direction.
teaser: Corn shrugs off a 35% jump in old-crop stocks and holds the round number anyway.

one_number.unit: year-over-year jump in Sept 1 corn stocks
one_number.context: USDA's Grain Stocks report showed 2.10 billion old-crop corn bushels on hand, up 35% from last year; soybean stocks fell 3% the same day.

sections.title: Corn Shrugs Off Heavy Stocks
sections.body:
- Corn held **$5.00**, up 3 cents, even though USDA's Grain Stocks report put old-crop bushels 35% above last year.
- That's a bearish number on paper, but the overnight trade didn't blink, basis at seasonal lows is already pricing the big old-crop pile.
sections.so_what: The market already knew the corn was there; the close says so.

sections.title: Beans Firm On Tighter Stocks
sections.body:
- Soybeans gained a nickel to **$12.86**, helped by a Sept 1 stocks figure down 3% from a year ago, the opposite signal from corn.
- Soybean meal added 0.3% to $345.90, soybean oil was flat at $68.94, so beans led the complex on their own number, not on products.
sections.so_what: Tighter bean stocks against a bigger corn pile is the whole spread story today.

sections.title: Cattle Soft, Crude Breaks Lower
sections.body:
- Live cattle slipped 0.7% to **$217.25** and feeders eased 0.2% to $333.85, both still digesting a beef cutout that's been drifting lower.
- Crude dropped sharply, down 2.4% to $87.26, even as Gulf exports recovered to 81% of pre-war levels, more barrels moving, not fewer.
sections.so_what: Diesel isn't following crude down, and combines still need diesel more than crude.

outside_the_pit.title: Gulf oil exports back near pre-war pace
outside_the_pit.body: Persian Gulf crude exports hit 81% of pre-war levels last month even as Hormuz traffic stays thin, Standard Chartered says, part of why crude broke lower today.

watch_list.desc: Export sales; corn over 1.2 MMT keeps today's stocks number from mattering much longer.
Harvest pace in the rain; corn below $5.00 opens the door if combines stay parked and basis widens.
Watch whether $6.32 diesel holds even if crude keeps breaking below $87.26.
